comparison: Perfect agreement on claims C37-C43. Both evaluations find the knockdown characterization well-supported by qPCR, western blotting, polysome profiling, and growth curves. No concerns raised by either evaluation.
Perfect agreement on claims C92-C93. Both evaluations support the DAP5-related findings showing similar effects across eIF3 knockdowns. Peer reviewers do not challenge these observations.

Both evaluations express uncertainty about claims C100-C104. OpenEval marks C103-C104 as hypotheses lacking experimental validation. Peer Reviewer 2 explicitly identifies difficulty reconciling differences between eIF3e and eIF3d knockdown, finding the explanation inadequate.

Strong agreement on claims C78-C80, C106 regarding MAPK pathway activation. Both evaluations find the evidence compelling. Peer reviewers explicitly acknowledge this as a key contribution with elevated ERK/c-Jun phosphorylation despite protein downregulation.

Agreement on claims C57-C59 regarding lysosomal and ER protein pathway enrichment. Both evaluations support the KEGG enrichment findings. Peer reviewers acknowledge increased TE of lysosomal and ER transcripts without methodological concerns.

Agreement on claims C61-C66 regarding ribosomal protein production and TOP mRNA translation. Both evaluations support the findings. Peer reviewers confirm upregulation of TOP mRNAs and ribosomal proteins, extending previous reports on eIF3d/e control of 5'TOP translation.

Agreement on claims C44-C51 regarding Ribo-seq quality metrics and differential expression analysis. Both evaluations find the technical approach convincing. Peer reviewers note 'convincing methods, data, and analyses' and accept the overlap patterns between eIF3d/e knockdowns.

Agreement on claims C44-C46 regarding Ribo-seq data quality. Both evaluations support the technical rigor. Peer reviewers provide comprehensive validation of RNA and ribosome footprinting data quality.

Agreement on claims C52-C55 regarding Venn diagram overlap patterns. Both evaluations support these findings. Peer reviewers accept the shared dysregulated transcripts between eIF3d/e knockdowns without challenge.

Agreement on claims C83-C87 regarding ISR pathway and reinitiation. Both evaluations support the findings on ATF4 and MDM2. Peer reviewers confirm this as important confirmatory work, though note lack of additional experimental evidence for Raf-1 uORF dependence.
Agreement on claims C88-C90 regarding footprint accumulation patterns at ATF4 and MDM2 uORFs. Both evaluations support these mechanistic findings as consistent with prior literature on reinitiation.

Agreement on claims C94-C99 regarding uORF correlation analysis. Both evaluations support the statistical findings. Peer reviewers acknowledge the role of eIF3 in reinitiation and translation of uORF-containing mRNAs.

Agreement on claims C72-C73, C76 regarding MAPK pathway component downregulation. Both evaluations support these findings as part of the coordinated regulation by eIF3 d/e, with peer reviewers explicitly acknowledging this contribution.
Agreement on claims C69, C71 regarding TOP mRNA differential effects and mTORC1-independent mechanism. Both evaluations support the evidence for this mechanistic distinction.
Agreement on claim C70 regarding mTORC1-independent regulation. Both evaluations support this finding without challenge, with peer reviewers accepting the data-driven conclusions.
Agreement on claim C74 regarding translational buffering. Both evaluations support this observation as a valid data-driven conclusion without methodological concerns.
Agreement on claim C60 regarding correlation between DTEG counts and phenotype severity. Both evaluations support this finding as part of the broader pathway enrichment analysis.

OpenEval supports claims C113-C114 regarding cross-study convergence with Lin et al. data on lysosome/ER pathways. No corresponding peer review evaluation found addressing this specific cross-study comparison.
OpenEval supports claim C124 regarding overlap between eIF3 binding sites and altered TE transcripts. No corresponding peer review evaluation found addressing this validation analysis.

OpenEval expresses uncertainty about claims C127-C130 regarding PRRC2 autoregulation, noting speculation lacks experimental validation. No corresponding peer review evaluation found addressing PRRC2 specifically.
OpenEval supports claims C1-C36 as well-established background knowledge with appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, as these are contextual rather than novel findings.

Both evaluations express uncertainty about broader implications. OpenEval marks claims C110, C129, C134 as speculative hypotheses lacking validation. Peer reviewers question physiological significance (editor) and request clearer models linking findings to biological outcomes (Reviewers 1, 3).

Peer reviewers question physiological and pathological significance of gene expression changes (claims C131-C132), requesting clearer models and exploration of impact on cell behavior. OpenEval addresses related speculative claims (C110, C129, C134) but not these specific claims about physiological significance.
